findings.trigger: After an otherwise valid CPU8 run, supply a hashed external completion receipt containing the matching freeze, manifest and tool-binding hashes, valid times, and restoration_verified/tool_exit_verified=true, without performing remote restoration.
findings.effect: The verifier returns CPU8_INTEGRATION_PASS. It never authenticates an archive/download receipt or restoration recomputation report; relocated is unused.
findings.recommendation: Require and verify external archive, download and restoration evidence bound to this sealed manifest, including packaged-verifier identity and matching recomputation results. Otherwise retain PENDING_DELIVERY.

findings.trigger: The permitted continuation loop accumulates more than 3000 observed descendant starts or 21600 seconds of covered process lifetimes before another formal admission.
findings.effect: Admission checks sources, wall time and instantaneous resources, but no cumulative process ceiling. Heartbeat counters are null, and verify_cpu8 likewise does not enforce these retained limits.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile unique PID/creation identities and covered lifetime charges across retained attempts, then enforce cumulative ceilings at admission and final verification. Preserve unobserved lifecycle fields as UNKNOWN.

findings.trigger: Archive a permitted, nearly incompressible 450 MiB sealed tree, or repeat archive creation into different external directories.
findings.effect: The logical-size check permits outputs that consume the required 256 MiB reserve, exceed task-wide storage during download/restoration, or create more than two complete archives. External outputs are outside the monitored root and have no cumulative accounting.
findings.recommendation: Account for external archives, downloads and restoration allocation against the shared task budget before writing; enforce the reserve, free-disk threshold and two-copy ceiling.

findings.trigger: A sealed-tree file is an NTFS hard link to another file inside or outside the root.
findings.effect: Inventory, membership and packaging accept it because only symlinks and junctions are rejected. The alias-free sealing requirement is therefore not enforced.
findings.recommendation: Apply the existing legacy hard-link rule to sealed evidence: reject regular files whose st_nlink is not one, in both packaging and verification.

scope.coverage: Current protocol; all candidate/source and candidate/src/rev2 files; legacy host, acceptance, C#, configuration and historical approval data; Windows startup, identity, exceptions and Job cleanup; source/freeze/continuation budgets; eight CPU8 paths and negative controls; process conversion, D0 replay, monitoring, tool binding, sealing and external delivery.
scope.input_identities: All 726 manifest entries matched size and SHA256; no unlisted supplied inputs beyond REVIEW_CONTEXT.md and the manifest. Acquisition comparison identified only the three documented onsite source changes. All four pinned tool identities matched. Final rehash found no input drift.

limitations: Read-only review without delegation or project code, test, script or native-library execution.
Supplied native/D0 evidence was inspected, not rerun; this is not native acceptance.
Post-verdict approvals, bindings and final startup artifacts remain pending by design. No formal freeze or CPU8 run has occurred.
Historical approvals remain historical; retained failures and missing outer OS lifecycle evidence remain unchanged and UNKNOWN.
